title: Scripts That Take Arguments
description: Write greet.sh that greets its first argument and fails politely with a usage message when called without one.
scenario: The support team wants a tiny greeting tool for their onboarding emails: /home/intern/greet.sh must print 'Hello, <name>!' when given a name as the first argument, and when called without an argument it must print a 'Usage: greet.sh <name>' line and exit with a non-zero status so their automation can detect the mistake.
symptoms: Calling the script with a name should print 'Hello, Sam!' but nothing exists yet
Calling it with no argument must NOT print a greeting
Support automation checks exit codes — a missing argument must exit non-zero
The usage message must mention 'Usage' so humans recognise it
mission: Create /home/intern/greet.sh: with an argument it prints 'Hello, <name>!'; without one it prints 'Usage: greet.sh <name>' and exits 1.

hints.title: First argument is $1
hints.content: `$1` holds the first positional parameter; `"$1"` (quoted) is safe even when it is empty.

hints.title: Test for empty
hints.content: `if [ -z "$1" ]` is true when the argument is missing or empty. `-z` means zero-length.

hints.title: Exit codes
hints.content: `exit 1` ends the script with failure status. The caller sees it in `$?` — 0 means success, anything else means failure.

hints.title: Wire it together
hints.content: echo the usage line BEFORE exiting so humans see why the script failed.

acceptance_criteria.description: calling greet.sh without an argument exits non-zero
the no-argument run prints a Usage message
